open_errors.issue: In ch 14 Neela weighs that going to the narrows leaves the meeting stone's cup empty a second night, after the fever night. Nothing shows her marking it later. Yet ch 16 says she has missed the stone only once ('the night of his fever'), and in ch 18 Ammu counts only the fever night plus the three bare nights of ch 16 to 17. The narrows night is missing from both counts.
open_errors.fix: In ch 14, where she goes 'by the long way to the cleft in the rocks under the second spur', add one line: she passes the meeting stone first and drags her cheek across the cup, late but marked.

open_errors.issue: Neela recalls that 'the warden had broken one tally open in the hall and said it wasn't enough.' In ch 4 Devan says only that the wax is genuine council wax and never says one is not enough. The 'need a second' idea is Asha's note, which Neela has not seen.
open_errors.fix: In ch 14, change the line to: 'The warden had broken one tally open in the hall. One tally was a story; two were a case.'

open_errors.issue: In ch 10 Janu gives the fort's theories about the barred shutters: Bhaskaran's lads say privacy, Gopan says Janu's old tale, Janu herself says the damp, and Chinna runs the wager. Ch 31 repeats that set (damp-madness, privacy, Janu's old tale). Ch 16 instead says Bhaskaran's lads called it damp-madness and Janu called it shyness.
open_errors.fix: In ch 16, change the sentence to: 'Bhaskaran's lads called it privacy, Gopan called it Janu's old tale, Janu called it the damp, and Chinna ran a wager on it at the kitchen door.'

open_errors.issue: In ch 12 Sudhi rides 'with the palace green on his sleeve'. In ch 17 Devan says no one looks in the bag of 'a man in royal blue'. Blue is the registry courier's colour in ch 8, not Sudhi's.
open_errors.fix: In ch 17, change 'a man in royal blue' to 'a man in palace green'.

open_errors.issue: In ch 20 Devan leaves his grey stone on the sill and keeps Kannan's white pebble as his cheek stone ('Keep Kannan's. It's the clean one.'). In ch 22 he takes 'the grey pebble from his pouch'.
open_errors.fix: In ch 22, change 'take the grey pebble from his pouch' to 'take the white pebble from his pouch'.

open_errors.issue: On reading the slip, Neela thinks of Ittan as 'the man who had proposed the match'. Nothing has shown her this. Only Devan knows Ittan's name stood first on the council letter (ch 23), and Ittan says it aloud only in ch 28.
open_errors.fix: In ch 22, replace 'the man who had proposed the match' with 'the man whose letter had asked so warmly after the warden's bride'.

open_errors.issue: Ammu's Valli cloth and resin pouch are found in the roots of the tree where she died, 'cached there before dusk'. In ch 26 to 27, though, Ammu is in the kennel and yard with Neela right up to sunset, and she turns on the cook-house roof. She had no time to reach the tree line before dusk.
open_errors.fix: In ch 28, change 'She had cached it there before dusk' to 'Muthu had found it at the cook-house corner, where she had shed it, and laid it at the tree.'

open_errors.issue: Devan says the hounds 'went to the kennel within a few nights' of the second dusk. Ch 3 (night two) already has them behind a kennel door, ch 4 says 'every night since your wedding', and ch 16 says 'from the second night'.
open_errors.fix: In ch 30, change 'The hounds went to the kennel within a few nights, the sentry after them' to 'The hounds went to the kennel that same night, the sentry a few nights after.'

open_errors.issue: Watching Muthu give Sudhi a grey-sealed letter, Neela notes 'She had seen it three times now.' She has never witnessed one before: the ch 12 handoff is in Devan's POV while she is at supper in the hall.
open_errors.fix: In ch 17, change 'She had seen it three times now.' to 'It was the first time she had seen it, though Janu teased him about his mother's post.'
